subject: ventures/youtube-revenue-rpm-analyzer
professional: a YouTube channel manager / MCN revenue analyst who reads Studio Advanced-mode exports weekly; first checks: does a real Studio Content 'Table data.csv' parse (Content + Video title columns, Total row on line 2, quoted 'Jun 18, 2024' publish dates, 3-decimal revenue, thousands separators after an Excel re-save, semicolon/UTF-16 locale re-saves), is RPM computed the way YouTube Help defines it (total estimated revenue after YouTube's share / total views x 1000, not CPM, which is advertiser cost per 1000 ad impressions before the 55% long-form / 45% Shorts partner share), and are Shorts separated from long-form before anything is benchmarked.

evidence.correctness: Independent script /tmp/claude-0/audit-youtube-rpm/indep.py (stdlib csv, does not import or read calc.mjs) on the built-in sample: channel RPM 4.4921 (754.95 / 168060 x 1000), median row RPM over rows >= 100 views 4.6933, one row under half the median (chalk line trick) with gap 180.12, under-fed rows remodel/tile/ghosting, impression-weighted CTR 3.771% (simple mean 3.65%), 4 rows for 80% and top share 0.4217, 0.0932 per watch hour, 7.42 subs per 1000 views. Subject via /tmp/claude-0/audit-youtube-rpm/subj.mjs (drives calc.mjs exactly as index.html run() does): identical on every figure (rpm 4.492145..., median 4.69326, rpmGap 180.12, ctr 0.03771, rowsFor80 4). Same totals (168060 views, 754.95, RPM 4.4922, median 4.6933) on six re-encodings of a Studio-shaped Content export: plain (quoted 'Jun 18, 2024' dates, a title with a comma, 3-decimal revenue, RPM and CPM columns), Excel US re-save with "48,210" and "1,318.401", European semicolon with 48.210 / 318,401, minimal semicolon EUR file with only 3-decimal revenue, US file with grouped views and 3-decimal revenue, UTF-16LE tab. RPM definition matches YouTube Help (revenue after share / all views x 1000). Not 4: a Date x Video file is analysed as 6 separate 'videos' (wrong row counts and findings), and month-name dates are unreadable.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features run end to end on test files: per-row RPM (pass), concentration (pass), under-half-median gap (pass), under-fed rows (pass), impression-weighted CTR gap (pass), RPM by length (pass), country mix (subject test plus own run), month-over-month for ISO by-day files (subject test), Total-row reconciliation (pass, 754.953 vs 754.95 no warning; 70% case warns), comma/tab/semicolon and UTF-16 (pass). Partial: 'a by-day chart export gets a month-over-month view' fails when dates are written 'Jun 18, 2024' (files/G_day_monthname.csv: 'No rows could be read', 28 rows skipped 'unreadable date'), and VENTURE.yaml:76-78 says column names are from memory and no real export was ever read. No stubs or TODOs; usage counting present.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject root: 32 tests pass in 0.15 s. Five seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 4 SURVIVED (median of an even count -> upper middle, calc.mjs:198; under-fed threshold 1.5 -> 1.2 x median, :281; Shorts bucket 60 s -> 180 s, :213; Total-reconciliation tolerance 1% -> 5%, :244), 1 caught (zero-revenue rows admitted to the low-RPM list, :268). The median, the core benchmark, is unpinned because the rpmGap test computes its expectation from r.medianRpm itself (calc.test.mjs:44). Parsing tests are decent (UTF-16, BOM, decimal comma, skipped lines).
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (382 lines), index.html script, calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs head. Pure functions, no network, careful number/decimal detection. Defects: comment at calc.mjs:59-61 describes durations ('"23" (minutes)', two parts read as h:mm) above parseWhen and contradicts parseDuration (seconds, mm:ss); ALIASES cpm and published (calc.mjs:130,132) are matched but never used and rpmGiven (:190) is read and discarded; fmt (:203) re-implements money's negative-sign logic; analyze() is one ~125-line function with UI copy inline; any row whose label is 'Total' is consumed as the Total row, so a video titled 'Total' vanishes silently and a second one overwrites the first (files/J_video_named_total.csv: 2 of 4 rows kept, no warning).
evidence.claims: Checked: FAQ 'RPM is what you earn per thousand views after YouTube's share ... CPM is what advertisers pay per thousand ad impressions before that share' matches YouTube Help definitions (pass); 'file never uploaded' (pass, no fetch/XHR in index.html, page.test.mjs); disclaimer and independence clause (pass); 'Rows that cannot be read are listed with a line number' (pass); 'Tests: node --test' (pass, 32 OK). Fail: index.html:62 says 'Duration and RPM are used when present' while index.html:99 says 'The RPM column in Studio, if present, is not used' and calc.mjs never uses rpmGiven. Partial: README:17 by-day chart export claim unverified against a real export (VENTURE.yaml:76 admits none was read) and fails on month-name dates; index.html:105 lists 'memberships and other revenue types outside the file' as not modelled, but Studio's Estimated revenue already includes memberships, Super Chat and Premium, so those are in the file and in every RPM shown.
evidence.fitness: Walked the analyst's job: export Content table, drop it in, get RPM per video ranked with findings. That works and adds value over Studio's own RPM column (concentration, gap sizing, CTR gap). Gaps hit in the first hour: Shorts are benchmarked against long-form (the sample's 45 s Short is flagged 'high' with a $180 gap and '8 to 20 min videos earn 19.8 times the RPM of up to 1 min'), a Date x Video export is not aggregated per video, no period-over-period or multi-channel merge (an MCN's core need), no revenue-source split, no CPM / monetized-playback view. A single creator could use it as a first look; a channel manager would still pivot by hand.
evidence.domain: Matches practice on: RPM = estimated revenue / views x 1000 over all views (YouTube Help 'RPM'), impression-weighted CTR, gap labelled a ceiling. Departs: Shorts and long-form share revenue differently (YPP terms: 55% of net ad revenue for long-form watch-page ads vs 45% of the allocated Shorts pool) and Shorts RPMs are structurally a fraction of long-form, so a single median benchmark and 'under half the median' findings across both are not how an analyst would read the file; the length bucket 'up to 1 min' uses the pre-15-Oct-2024 Shorts limit (Shorts may now run to 3 min); the benchmark is the unweighted median of row RPMs rather than a views-weighted or per-format benchmark.

defects.what: Shorts and long-form are benchmarked against one median: a Short is flagged 'high' with a sized RPM gap ($180.12 on the sample) and the length finding compares long-form with Shorts RPM (19.8x), though their revenue pools and shares differ (55% vs 45%); duration is available to separate them

Median row RPM, the core benchmark, is unpinned: replacing the even-count median with the upper middle leaves all tests green, because the rpmGap test computes its expectation from r.medianRpm itself; the 1.5x under-fed threshold and the 1% Total tolerance also survive mutation
A Date x Video export (one row per video per day) is analysed as separate videos: rows are not aggregated by label, so row counts, the median and every per-video finding are wrong, with no warning

Never checked against a real Studio export: column names and the by-day chart format are from memory (VENTURE.yaml says so), and month-name dates ('Jun 18, 2024', Studio's own publish-time format) make a by-day file unreadable ('No rows could be read')
Page says 'Duration and RPM are used when present' while the model section (line 99) says the Studio RPM column is not used; calc.mjs reads rpmGiven and never uses it

'Not modelled: ... memberships and other revenue types outside the file' implies those are excluded, but Studio's Estimated revenue already includes memberships, Super Chat and Premium, so they are inside every RPM shown
Any row labelled 'Total' is taken as the Total row: a video titled 'Total' disappears silently and a second one overwrites the first
Stale comment above parseWhen describes durations ('23' as minutes, two parts as h:mm), contradicting parseDuration (seconds, mm:ss); cpm and published aliases and rpmGiven are dead
Length bucket 'up to 1 min' uses the pre-2024-10-15 Shorts limit; Shorts may now run to 3 minutes, so Shorts land in '1 to 8 min'

verdict: The arithmetic is right: an independent stdlib script reproduces channel RPM 4.4921, median row RPM 4.6933, the 180.12 gap, impression-weighted CTR 3.771% and the concentration figures exactly, and a Studio-shaped Content export parses to the same totals in six encodings (quoted month-name publish dates, thousands separators, European semicolons, UTF-16 tab). RPM and CPM are defined as YouTube Help defines them. It misses the bar on verification (4 of 5 seeded mutants survive, including the median that every finding rests on) and claims (the page contradicts itself on the RPM column and mislabels memberships as outside the file), and a channel manager would hit the domain gap at once: Shorts are benchmarked against long-form and flagged 'high', a Date x Video export is analysed as duplicate videos, and the parser has never met a real export.
